description:
Somos "Inges sobrevivIEEEndo", un equipo de 6 líderes IEEE (UPS, ESPE, Yachay, UTN). Combinamos mecatrónica (hardware/robótica), telecomunicaciones (conectividad) y computación (software).

¿Por qué unirte? Tenemos experiencia real liderando y gestionando proyectos tecnológicos. Sabemos resolver problemas bajo presión y llevar ideas del prototipo al software.

Buscamos: Mentes en Diseño UI/UX, Storytelling o Ciencias de la Tierra para potenciar la solución.
summary:
AstroSalud is an autonomous, offline-first Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) and environmental monitoring console engineered for long-duration human spaceflight (Artemis and Mars transit). During deep space missions, communication delays between 5 and 22 minutes make real-time telemedicine with Earth Mission Control impossible. AstroSalud addresses this challenge by running entirely at the edge on an energy-efficient 7-inch Raspberry Pi touchscreen.

The system tracks vital physiological telemetry (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, temperature, glucose, radiation dose) alongside spaceship ECLSS and rover habitat parameters. Utilizing governed machine learning algorithms (scikit-learn SGD/Ridge), it forecasts 7-day health trends and provides personalized, actionable countermeasures. Crucially, AstroSalud introduces a strict Human-in-the-Loop clinical governance pipeline: AI models never train on unverified telemetry. Every update requires Chief Medical Officer (CMO) review via a PIN-protected queue, generating validated candidate models before deployment. With a WCAG 2.1 AA high-contrast, colorblind-friendly interface, AstroSalud guarantees crew autonomy and medical resilience.
details: S.I.M.E. (Sistema Integral de Monitoreo Espacial) is an autonomous, offline Edge AI health and telemetry monitoring system designed for long-duration deep space missions. Developed by team "Inges sobrevivIEEEndo", S.I.M.E. addresses the critical challenge of communication latency and isolation during interplanetary travel. Operating locally on a Raspberry Pi 5 architecture, the system continuously monitors key NASA-defined space hazards, including environmental telemetry (CO2, radiation, and suit pressure drops to prevent nitrogen gas embolism/decompression sickness) alongside crew vital signs (Heart Rate, SpO2, and automated time-based bone/muscle fatigue modeling). Utilizing a Python-based MLP Classifier neural network combined with deterministic safety failsafes, S.I.M.E. diagnoses anomalies in real-time without terrestrial reliance, triggers immediate onboard hardware alerts, and autonomously compiles mission status reports.
